The original full pre-consent dependency simulation remains unrecoverable and explicitly documented.

phases.title: Doctor, management, and recovery
phases.summary: P3 remains active; P0-P2 are accepted complete. Core Doctor, default-deny management, operation journal/recovery, backup/restore fixture gates, and fail-closed provider checks are source/fixture complete under the cited historical evidence. The native desktop manager now requests the Termux:X11 Android activity after X11/XFCE readiness and reports request outcome separately while keeping gui_visible=unknown; native boot uses the same manager path. Read-only native/GUI-off boot previews both report ready and changed=false; current boot profile remains default cli-only. Latest RB06 postboot checkpoint is verified_reboot_service_unqualified / NOT_READY, with the native desktop absent after reboot; authenticated 8023 afterward does not qualify the checkpoint. ADB from the authorized Linux PRoot-Distro host force-stopped Termux:X11; with it closed, a native 8022 manager retry was still rejected, confirming that an already-open activity was not the cause. Remaining P3 gates: native cold-boot/activity fallback qualification, SSH listener ownership/bind evidence, and Shizuku Binder/permission/watchdog/provider identity. The read-only Doctor now adds an upstream server process-name hint, with current 8022 evidence recorded. Actual Ternux PRoot parity is P4; hybrid routing is P8. The latest activity-request implementation has syntax and preview checks but no test-suite run or reboot/UI launch. Live native manager check: stale session was reconciled without signaling absent processes, then X11/XFCE started on :2; Android activity request was rejected and GUI visibility remains unknown. Existing :1 socket/lock points to PID 24612 not visible to ps, so artifacts were preserved. Default CLI-only boot remains unchanged. Native SSH 8022 is wildcard/password-enabled by config, but listener owner and reachability remain unknown; 8023 is a distinct verified loopback Runit service. Follow-up found that the native Termux am wrapper succeeds where /system/bin/am is rejected. The manager now uses that wrapper; after ADB force-stop a native 8022 start returned activity_request=accepted, and ADB confirmed MainActivity resumed (PID 17642). A guarded stale-artifact recovery then removed the positively stale same-UID :1 lock/socket pair (PID 24612 absent; socket refused connections) and restarted native desktop on :1. Current status is running with supervisor/X11/XFCE present; gui_visible remains unknown. Owner confirmed CLI, X11 GUI, and local Web UI must manage the same provider-scoped resources through one shared management layer; accepted architecture and serial implementation gates are recorded in ADR-0004 and SHARED-MANAGEMENT-PLAN. The first shared PRoot GUI management slice is source/fixture complete: typed app launch and shortcut list/preview/apply operations route CLI, desktop entries, and the X11 shortcut manager through one service. Exact existing legacy launchers are recognized, while customized entries stay conflicts. Live read-only inventory over native 8022 preserved the existing Terminal/Files conflicts; no menu or GUI process was changed. Updated GUI interaction and Web/session client remain pending. Shared management inventory and read-only Doctor service entry now cover SSH/Runit, runtimes, boot/background, recovery, add-on/plugin/tool and API-backend maturity. PRoot lifecycle scope is recorded as planned: adapt installed Debian first, then selective distro and desktop installs/removal. Cloud API remains disabled. P0 audit fixes at 4eed13a: 301/301 Native Termux tests pass; lifecycle guards, JSON serialization, and atomic state helpers are corrected. Current SSH/service and reboot qualification limits are recorded in the linked audit snapshot.
phases.next_action: Resolve the installed 8023 Runit definition drift with an owner-reviewed rollback plan; separately establish listener ownership and preserve the 8022 manual development channel. Continue P3 management/recovery gates; do not claim reboot qualification without an owner-approved reboot.

phases.title: Existing Ternux PRoot feature-parity provider
phases.summary: Read-only Ternux source/state and guest diagnostics record v1.4.0, configured guest account, Zink backend, and launcher display :0. Same-input :0 handoff is partial while :1 verifies; Ternux reported running while current visible server :1 matched Ternuxx ownership and :0 was not observed (installed-script identity unverified); active :0 rootfs/X-server ownership and feature parity remain unverified, so no lifecycle adapter is qualified. Guest diagnostics now explain the observed :0 process mismatch while :1 still verifies; Ternux ownership remains unverified. Fresh native installed CLI recheck at 08:21 UTC confirms Ternux v1.4.0 exposes no generic workload execution command; host backend is Zink/Vulkan but renderer is unknown. P4 remains planned pending the P3 ownership contract and owner review of ADR-0006. A fresh native bounded verification at 08:23 UTC passed on :1/Zink-Turnip/audio control, but does not establish rootfs/session ownership or workload dispatch.
